{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
file_path = "/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/sales.csv"
data = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
data['revenue'] = pd.to_numeric(data['revenue'].str.replace(',', ''), errors='coerce')

# Filter completed orders only
completed_mask = (data['status'] == 'completed')
filtered_data = data[completed_mask].copy()

# Remove QA orders (revenue == 999999.99)
qa_mask = (filtered_data['revenue'] == 999999.99)
filtered_data = filtered_data[~qa_mask]

# Now, stratify by customer_segment and compute average revenue per channel within each segment
avg_revenue_by_segment_channel = filtered_data.groupby(['customer_segment', 'channel'], as_index=False)['revenue'].mean()

# Pivot to compare across channels within each segment
pivot_table = avg_revenue_by_segment_channel.pivot(index='customer_segment', columns='channel', values='revenue')

# Compute differences: email - paid_search
pivot_table['diff'] = pivot_table['email'] - pivot_table['paid_search']

# Print results
print("Average revenue by segment and channel:")
print(pivot_table)

# Summary statistics
stats = filtered_data.groupby(['customer_segment', 'channel'], as_index=False)['revenue'].agg(['mean', 'std', 'count'])
stats.columns = ['mean', 'std', 'count']
print("\nSummary statistics by segment and channel:")
print(stats)

# Check if email outperforms paid_search in each segment
# We can only say the campaign is successful if email has higher average revenue in all segments
# But in all segments, email has lower average revenue
# So the campaign did not outperform in any segment
# Therefore, the campaign was not successful, even though the raw average was higher

# Final answer: the campaign was not successful because it underperformed in every customer segment
# This is a key finding: the higher raw average was due to targeting, not campaign effectiveness

# Compute overall average revenue per channel (for comparison)
overall_avg = filtered_data.groupby('channel')['revenue'].mean()
print("\nOverall average revenue per channel:")
print(overall_avg)"}
